title: RBI Holds Rates Steady, Raises India's GDP Growth Forecast to 6.7% Amid Oil and Inflation Risks
excerpt: The central bank's fourth consecutive pause at 5.25% comes with a modest growth upgrade and lower inflation projections, but economists remain divided on how long the hold can last.
body:
• The RBI's monetary policy committee voted unanimously to hold the repo rate at 5.25% for the fourth consecutive meeting, while raising the FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.7% from 6.6%.
  • Annual inflation projections were lowered to 5.0% from 5.1%, with core inflation cut more steeply to 4.3% from 4.7%, though headline inflation is expected to peak in the third quarter.
  • Governor Sanjay Malhotra cited resilient domestic demand, robust exports, and expanding manufacturing as evidence that India remains the world's fastest-growing major economy.
  • Some economists expect rate hikes of up to 75 basis points by early 2027 if oil prices remain elevated, while others see tightening beginning no sooner than December.

The Reserve Bank of India held interest rates steady on Wednesday and nudged up its growth forecast for the fiscal year, striking a cautiously optimistic tone even as the Middle East conflict keeps energy costs elevated and inflation above target.

Unanimous Hold, Modest Upgrade

The six-member monetary policy committee voted unanimously to keep the repo rate at 5.25%, extending its pause to four consecutive meetings. At the same time, the RBI raised its real GDP growth projection for FY27 — the year ending March 2027 — to 6.7% from the 6.6% forecast in June, according to the Wall Street Journal.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-Va3BsnILmM

The upgrade was modest but deliberate. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said growth "continues to be supported by resilient domestic demand, sustained expansion in manufacturing and services activity, and robust exports, reaffirming India's position as the world's fastest-growing major economy."

"Growth continues to be supported by resilient domestic demand, sustained expansion in manufacturing and services activity, and robust exports, reaffirming India's position as the world's fastest-growing major economy."

— Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, Reserve Bank of India

Inflation: Lower Forecast, Persistent Risk

On the inflation front, the RBI revised its annual projection down to 5.0% from 5.1%, with the core inflation forecast — excluding food and fuel — cut more sharply to 4.3% from 4.7%, according to Reuters.

Retail inflation crossed the RBI's 4% medium-term target for the first time in 17 months in June but remains within the central bank's 2-6% tolerance band. The RBI expects headline inflation to rise in the near term as food and fuel costs climb, peaking in the third quarter before moderating.

The key risk remains oil. Restricted flows through the Strait of Hormuz, a consequence of renewed U.S.-Iran military tensions, have pushed up energy prices that directly feed into India's import bill. The rupee has weakened more than 6% against the dollar this year, partly reflecting those pressures.

Mixed Signals From the Economy

High-frequency indicators paint a divided picture. The purchasing managers' index slipped to a five-year low, suggesting manufacturing momentum has softened. But credit demand is growing at a much stronger pace of nearly 18%, and the services sector continues to expand, Reuters reported.

The government has deployed supply-side measures — including higher import duties on silver and gold and currency intervention via foreign-exchange swap windows — to conserve reserves and prioritize essential imports like crude.

"Given the supply-side measures undertaken primarily by the government of India, inflation seems to be under control, and this provides the RBI with significant headroom to maintain a neutral stance and keep rates unchanged," said Ajitabh Bharti, co-founder of CapitalXB.

Rate Hikes on the Horizon?

Despite the dovish signaling, the debate over how long the RBI can hold is intensifying. Capital Economics believes the central bank will be forced to tighten, forecasting 75 basis points of hikes to bring the repo rate to 6.00% by early 2027.

"We still think that rising inflation will leave the central bank with little choice but to tighten monetary policy over the coming months," said Shilan Shah, deputy chief emerging markets economist at Capital Economics.

Others are less hawkish. Rahul Bajoria of BofA Global Research expects any tightening to begin no earlier than December, given the governor's dovish messaging and improving growth-inflation dynamics.

What It Means for NRI Investors

For NRI investors with exposure to Indian equities, debt, and real estate, the RBI's stance is a double-edged sword. Stable rates support asset prices and economic growth in the near term, but a sharp oil-driven tightening cycle later this year could pressure bond yields, compress equity valuations, and further weaken the rupee against the dollar — eroding returns for dollar-denominated investors.

The 6.7% GDP growth forecast, even if slower than the prior year, still positions India well ahead of most major economies and reinforces the case for long-term allocation to Indian markets.

What's Next

The next MPC meeting will be the most consequential in months. If oil prices stabilize and monsoon-related food inflation eases, the RBI may maintain its hold into early 2027. If not, a rate hike cycle could begin as soon as the December meeting, with significant implications for borrowers, markets, and the rupee.
